Definition: Affordability of mobile broadband data, measured as the cost of a basic mobile data plan (1-2GB) as a percentage of GNI per capita. The UN Broadband Commission target is below 2% of monthly GNI per capita. Affordability is the single largest barrier to internet adoption in Africa.
revision_notes: The cited A4AI 2019 report was read and confirms a 2016 national average cost of 10% of GNI per capita for 1GB (the figure the Value Code should logically rest on), plus a bottom-40%-income figure of 27-48% which the original Comments used to justify Code 1 (Very Expensive) - but the variable definition asks for the general basic-plan cost, not an income-quintile figure, so even on 2016 data alone Code 1 was a stretch (10% sits at the very top of the 'Expensive 5-10%' band, code 2, not >10%). More importantly, the evidence is nine years stale. Fresher data: Cable.co.uk's 2023 global mobile-data-pricing survey (5,600 plans, 237 countries; reported via SA Mobile, June 2025) puts Mozambique's average price for 1GB at USD 0.78. Against World Bank GNI per capita, Atlas method, of USD 540 in 2023 (macrotrends.net, sourced from World Bank WDI), monthly GNI per capita is USD 45, so USD 0.78 is approximately 1.7% of monthly GNI per capita - within the 'Affordable (1-2%)' band, i.e. Code 4. A separate, more recent Cable.co.uk-based report (360Mozambique/Digital Banking News, 2025) cites an even lower USD 0.17/GB, which would compute to under 1% of GNI per capita (Code 5, the scale ceiling) - but this figure diverges sharply from the 2023 figure and its methodology/date could not be independently confirmed, so it is not relied upon here. Recalculating Code 4 on the more robustly dated 2023 cable.co.uk figure, cross-checked against World Bank GNI data, rather than guessing between two divergent recent price points. Flagged for human review given (a) the scale of change from Code 1 to Code 4, (b) the fact the % figure is derived by combining two separate sources rather than read directly from a single affordability report, and (c) the unresolved discrepancy with the even-lower 2025 price estimate.
revised_comments: Mozambique's basic mobile data plan is affordable relative to income. Cable.co.uk's 2023 global pricing survey puts the average cost of 1GB of mobile data in Mozambique at USD 0.78, equivalent to around 1.7% of monthly GNI per capita (World Bank GNI per capita, Atlas method, of USD 540 in 2023). This places Mozambique within the 'Affordable' band, below the UN Broadband Commission's 2% target threshold used for the top affordability categories, and a marked improvement on the 2016 national average of around 10% of GNI per capita reported by the Alliance for Affordable Internet. A more recent industry report citing an even lower price of USD 0.17/GB in 2025 suggests affordability may have continued to improve, though this figure has not been independently corroborated.

Definition: The country's total international internet bandwidth capacity per internet user, indicating the quality and capacity of the country's connection to the global internet. Determined by submarine cable landings (for coastal states), cross-border terrestrial fibre (for landlocked states), and satellite links.
revision_notes: The cited source (TheGlobalEconomy.com, sourcing ITU World Telecommunication/ICT Indicators data) was fetched and read. It reports Mozambique's international internet bandwidth per internet user at 9.16 kbit/s in 2016, the same figure quoted in the original row's Comments. Against the variable's own scale (1=Very Low <5 kbit/s; 2=Low 5-19 kbit/s), 9.16 kbit/s falls within the Low (5-19 kbit/s) band, not Very Low, so Code 1 does not match the cited evidence - it should be Code 2. Searched for fresher data (ITU DataHub, ITU World Telecommunication/ICT Indicators Database 2021-2023 editions, ITU LDC country profile for Mozambique) but found no more recent country-specific bandwidth-per-user figure; ITU appears not to have published an update for Mozambique on this indicator since 2016, and the WTID database was discontinued after the 2024 (2023 data) release without a Mozambique figure surfacing in available search results. The 2016 ITU estimate therefore remains the most recent traceable figure despite its age.
revised_comments: Mozambique's international internet bandwidth stood at 9.16 kilobits per second per internet user in 2016, according to ITU World Telecommunication/ICT Indicators data. This falls within the 'Low' band (5-19 kbit/s per user) rather than the lowest band, though it remains far below the global average of around 151 kbit/s per user for the same year. No more recent country-specific bandwidth-per-user estimate for Mozambique could be identified, reflecting a broader gap in publicly available, up-to-date data on this indicator for the country.
